standard.title: Select and use materials safely
standard.description: select and use materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions (AC9TDE2P02). They have used materials and tools in a supervised context. They have not yet selected materials with justified reasons, considered environmental impact across the production process, or used appropriate technologies terminology to describe procedures.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select and use materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions, with consideration of environmental impact and using appropriate terminology to describe procedures.

nodes.label: Selecting materials with reasons
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select materials and components for a design purpose and give reasons for their choices that reference material properties or sustainability
nodes.minimum_width: Select at least two materials for a design task and give one reason for each choice (referencing a property or sustainability consideration)
nodes.typical_width: Select materials, components and joining techniques for design tasks with reasons; consider environmental impact in selections — for example whether packaging and offcuts can be recycled; explain selections using technologies terms
wider: Select materials with explicit sustainability consideration — compare materials by compostability, recyclability and durability before choosing; document the selection reasoning

Explore material choices from products made in an Asian country (e.g. bamboo, different timber types, natural fibres) — compare to materials typically available locally and discuss how material availability shapes design decisions

response_modes.reason: Students often select materials based on appearance or familiarity rather than properties relevant to function and sustainability. Scaffolding the selection reasoning (identify the design requirement → identify which property matters → check the material has that property) builds deliberate material selection practice.

success_criteria: Names at least two materials chosen for the design
Gives at least one reason for each choice that references a property or sustainability factor
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who select materials without reasoning about properties make production decisions that can compromise function and safety — arbitrary selection cannot be remedied in N2 and N3 because material choices are already locked in.

nodes.label: Safe, responsible and cooperative making practices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate safe, responsible and inclusive work practices when using tools and equipment
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two safe work practices when using tools or equipment (e.g. correct grip, checking workspace is clear, appropriate handling of sharp equipment)
nodes.typical_width: Explain and apply safe, responsible, inclusive and cooperative work practices across different making contexts; use tools and equipment accurately when measuring, marking and cutting; explain why each safety practice matters
wider: Describe the safety practices relevant to making a specific engineered solution (e.g. a robotic device) — explain how safety practices change when tools and materials become more complex
Explore how digital tools (virtual reality, simulations) can be used to practise assembly before physical making — discuss what safety benefits this approach offers and what it does not replace

response_modes.reason: Safe work practices require habitual, precise application. Consolidation — consistent practice across making tasks, with feedback — is what builds reliable safety behaviour. Breadth of context matters less than accuracy and consistency of practice.

success_criteria: Applies at least two safe work practices without prompting
Uses at least one tool accurately (measuring, marking or cutting to a specified dimension)
nodes.hinge_reason: Safe work practices are a non-negotiable gate for all physical making — students who have not consolidated safe handling cannot proceed to production contexts in N3. This is a safety prerequisite, not a quality issue.

nodes.label: Using technologies terminology to describe procedures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the procedures and techniques used in making, using appropriate technologies terms
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two technologies terms correctly when describing a making procedure to another student
nodes.typical_width: Use appropriate technologies terms to describe and share procedures and techniques for making across different design contexts; include terms for materials, tools, components and processes
wider: Document a making procedure for a complex product (e.g. an engineered robotic device or a textile item) using technologies terms and steps clear enough for another student to follow
Create a visual or digital guide to a making procedure using appropriate terminology — evaluate whether the guide is clear enough for a peer who has not done the task before

response_modes.reason: Technologies terminology needs to be built across different materials, tools and making contexts. Students who only use terms in one context (e.g. woodwork) may not transfer them to textiles or food technology. Repertoire across making domains is the target.

success_criteria: Uses at least two technologies terms correctly in context
Procedural description is clear enough for another student to follow
